archetypes.name: Classify a Power Function
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.2 — Power Functions and Polynomial Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A power function has one term of the form kx^p with a real coefficient and fixed real exponent; a constant base with variable exponent describes a different family.
archetypes.mentalModel: Check which object varies: in a power function the variable is the base and the exponent stays fixed.
archetypes.governingRelation: f(x)=k x^p, where k and p are real constants

cognitiveTraps.description: Calling a constant base with variable exponent a power function.
Treating a sum of terms as a single power function.
Ignoring that the exponent itself changes with the input.
Reporting the coefficient as the fixed exponent in a single-term power function.

archetypes.figureNone: This is a symbolic family classification; a graph is not needed to distinguish variable base from constant base.

archetypes.name: Determine Power-Function End Behavior
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.2 — Identifying End Behavior of Power Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: For integer powers, parity determines whether both ends share a direction or oppose one another, and the coefficient sign determines whether the leading direction is reflected.
archetypes.mentalModel: Read the exponent parity first, then the coefficient sign; apply both to the left and right ends separately.

cognitiveTraps.description: Using the same left-end behavior for even and odd exponents.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: odd power has matching end directions

cognitiveTraps.description: Forgetting that a negative coefficient reflects the power graph across the x-axis.
cognitiveTraps.trapFormula: -x^5 has the end behavior of x^5

cognitiveTraps.description: Reversing the behavior as x approaches negative infinity and positive infinity.

archetypes.name: Identify a Polynomial Function
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.2 — Identifying Polynomial Functions
archetypes.coreConcept: A polynomial is a finite sum of terms whose variable exponents are nonnegative integers and whose coefficients are real constants.
archetypes.mentalModel: Inspect every term after simplification: each power must be a whole-number exponent at least zero, and the expression must be a finite sum.
archetypes.governingRelation: f(x)=a_nx^n+...+a_1x+a_0, n a nonnegative integer, a_n ≠ 0

cognitiveTraps.description: Allowing a negative variable exponent in a polynomial term.
Allowing a fractional variable exponent in a polynomial term.
Allowing the variable to appear in the exponent.

archetypes.figureNone: Polynomial status is determined by the finite algebraic form and exponent restrictions, not by a sketch.

archetypes.name: Read Degree and Leading Term
archetypes.source: OpenStax Algebra and Trigonometry 2e §5.2 — Identifying the Degree and Leading Coefficient
archetypes.coreConcept: After combining like terms, the greatest variable exponent determines polynomial degree; its term and coefficient are the leading term and leading coefficient.
archetypes.mentalModel: Simplify first, then search for the greatest exponent rather than the first written term; preserve the sign attached to its coefficient.
archetypes.governingRelation: degree(f)=max exponent with nonzero coefficient; leading term=a_n x^n

cognitiveTraps.description: Choosing the first written term instead of the term with greatest exponent.
